notes: This contract records Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Delay Subscription Evaluation behavior in the non-installable embedded development profile. The source semantic block is §8.1.8; the pinned Requirements Lab export gives these immutable candidates a stale annex display title and the erroneous §8.1.10 clause metadata, as recorded by RL-018. Enabled federations retain a joined non-source recipient route for ordinary Send Interaction and ordinary Update Attribute Values only when planning finds no current subscription, then project the recipient's current active subscription at the ordinary receive-order callback boundary or at the time-constrained TSO grant boundary. Each boundary is exercised under HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE: receive-order cases suspend/resume direct dispatch, and timestamped cases use direct Time Advance Grant delivery. The attribute-update cases establish a known object before dropping and restoring its attribute declaration, so they isolate subscription timing from discovery. Focused explicit-source regional attribute-update and regional interaction cases now extend the timestamped path: a passel accepted while its regional declaration is absent is delivered after the declaration is restored only when the federation-wide switch is enabled, while removing the declaration before a later grant suppresses the callback in both modes. The enabled and disabled switch modes re-evaluate a previously selected recipient immediately before an actual callback. This slice still excludes directed interactions, asynchronous-delivery timing, late join/resignation races, retraction edge cases, distributed transport, package/JUnit/protected-review evidence, and conformance.
